0.0.n: A conversational acknowledgment that opens the next part of the video.

0.2.n: With ことで, this forms a conversational transition rather than literally quoting something.

0.3.n: Literally a matter or thing; here it belongs to the transition ということで.

0.4.n: Completes ということで, which introduces what the speaker will do next.

0.5.n: Adds a friendly, conversational tone to the transition.

0.7.n: Tells when the speaker bought the products.

0.8.n: 買って is the linking form of 買う; きた adds coming back after buying.

1.0.n: Points to the products the speaker is presenting.

1.1.n: This is the first part of the brand name d'Alba, not a separate Japanese word.

1.3.n: This completes the brand name d'Alba.

1.4.n: Connects the brand name to its products.

1.5.n: A product name built from English loanwords, treated as one noun.

1.6.n: Joins the two products in the list.

1.7.n: A product description built from English loanwords.

1.8.n: Marks both products as what the speaker will use in the following line.

2.0.n: The Japanese says today, without specifically saying tonight.

2.1.n: は sets today as the topic, while ね adds a friendly conversational touch.

2.3.n: 使って plus いこう expresses moving ahead with using them; いこう is the intention form of いく.

2.4.n: Introduces the intention expressed before 思います.

2.5.n: Polite form of 思う; with an intention form plus と, it describes the speaker's plan.

3.0.n: Names the source of the damage.

3.1.n: Connects 熱 to ダメージ, explaining what causes the damage.

3.2.n: An English loanword referring here to harm to the hair.

3.3.n: Identifies ダメージ as what the products prevent.

3.4.n: 防いで is the linking form of 防ぐ; くれる presents the protection as a benefit to the speaker.

3.5.n: Introduces the reason for applying the products before drying.

4.0.n: Refers to the appliance, but with 前 it means before using it.

4.1.n: Follows ドライヤー to specify timing before blow-drying.

4.2.n: Presents before blow-drying as one possible suitable time.

4.4.n: A casual general-purpose verb meaning do; here it refers to applying the products.

4.5.n: Turns やる into an activity that can be described as good.

4.6.n: Marks applying the products at that time as what is being evaluated.

4.7.n: Describes applying the products before drying as advisable.

4.8.n: Combines with な to form かな, expressing a tentative thought.

4.9.n: Completes かな, softening the judgment rather than asking the viewer directly.

4.10.n: Marks いいかな as the thought expressed by 思う.

4.11.n: Plain form of 思う, followed by ので to give a reason.

4.12.n: Connects this reasoning to the speaker's plan in the next line.

5.0.n: Refers to the day of this routine, not explicitly the evening.

5.1.n: Makes today the topic of the plan.

5.2.n: With 前, this refers to the time before using the dryer.

5.3.n: Combines with ドライヤー and に to mean before blow-drying.

5.4.n: Marks before blow-drying as the time for using the products.

5.5.n: Adds a friendly pause without changing the basic message.

5.7.n: Points to the two products already introduced.

5.8.n: Combines with つ to count the products.

5.9.n: A general counting ending; 2つ counts two things without specifying a particular type.

5.10.n: Marks この2つ as what the speaker will use.

5.11.n: The linking form of 使う connects this step to the next part of the routine.

6.0.n: 後 adds after to ドライヤー, referring to finishing the drying step.

6.1.n: Marks after blow-drying as the time for the next application.

6.3.n: Introduces an additional product-use step, not repetition of the same product.

6.4.n: With の, describes a product separate from the two already mentioned.

6.5.n: Connects 別 to the noun ヘアミルク.

6.6.n: The first part of ヘアミルク, an English-based term for a hair-care product.

6.7.n: In ヘアミルク, this describes a milky hair-care product, not drinking milk.

6.8.n: Identifies the hair milk as what the speaker will apply.

6.9.n: The linking form of 使う continues the sequence into the final statement.

7.0.n: Repeats the timing as the speaker sums up the routine.

7.1.n: Sets today as the topic of the concluding plan.

7.2.n: An English loanword that combines with する to mean perform care.

7.3.n: The intention form of する; with と思います, it expresses the speaker's plan.

7.4.n: Links the intended action ケアしよう to 思います.

7.5.n: Polite form of 思う, completing the expression of intention しようと思います.

0.lit: All right, so, you know, bought and brought back today…
0.tip: 買ってきた describes the products named in the next line; it is not a future plan to buy.

1.lit: These d'Alba hair oil serum and hair perfume serum, as things to use…
1.tip: The final を marks both products as the objects of 使う in the next line.

2.lit: Today, you know, right away, I think I'll go ahead and use them.
2.tip: An intention form followed by と思います expresses a plan; 今日 means today, not specifically tonight.

3.lit: Because they prevent damage caused by heat for me…
3.tip: Adding くれる presents the products' action as helpful to the speaker.

4.lit: Since I think applying them before the dryer or such might be good…
4.tip: かな softens いい into a tentative judgment: might be good.

5.lit: Today, before the dryer, you know, using these two, and…
5.tip: 使って links this application to the next step rather than ending the sentence.

6.lit: After the dryer, also using a different hair milk, and…
6.tip: ドライヤー後 means after using the dryer, contrasting with ドライヤー前 earlier.

7.lit: Today, I think I'll do hair care.
7.tip: しようと思います is a polite way to state what you intend to do.
